scope: Synthetic local backup/restore qualification; no production access, provider calls, deployment, publication or physical cleanup activation.

fixes.behavior: Restore and rollback journal starting-target before startup; never automatically replace possibly accepted writes after startup/verification/terminal commit failure.
Require auth.sqlite and sync.sqlite in a valid streamed tar listing before live volume replacement; preserve tar failure status on legacy POSIX shells.

Refuse canonical committed FS metadata sidecars missing their blob payload entry under the archived FS root; preserve uncommitted uploads, temporary sidecars and opaque generation artifacts; no new format or physical cleanup.

walFrameFix.behavior: Stream complete current-generation SQLite WAL frames and verify cumulative checksums before native opening with one bounded page/frame buffer. Refuse damage without hiding committed records; preserve stale reset tails and incomplete appends.

walHeaderFix.behavior: Validate nonempty SQLite WAL headers before native opening, including magic, format, page size and documented endian-dependent checksum. Empty checkpointed WALs remain accepted. Actual malformed-header restore refusal safely recovers the committed WAL-only record.

restoreCapacityFix.behavior: Restore reclaim capacity uses allocated du -sk blocks converted to bytes; backup payload dataBytes remains apparent du -sb bytes. Sparse logical holes cannot authorize an over-capacity destructive restore.

nativeDatabaseFix.behavior: Use restored-image native readonly SQLite quick_check and require a nonempty schema in a network-denied helper after extraction and before startup. Refusal safely restores the pre-mutation snapshot; failed recovery retains journal. Initial after-start placement caught non-SQLite inputs but allowed empty schema initialization; do not apply initial commit alone.

remainingRisksAndNotTested: WAL header and current-generation full-frame checksum validation refuse reproduced malformed-header/frame-content omissions. Old-salt tails after reset and incomplete append tails retain SQLite recovery semantics. Complete same-generation frames with bad checksums are conservatively refused, including torn uncommitted frames; input is not repaired. Truncation or altered salts can still resemble legitimate interrupted/reused tails; expected record inventory remains unqualified.

Before 1ab5f45e, an authenticated archive missing only the referenced blob passed restore and deep health; actual download returned 404. That case is now refused. When both blob and sidecar are absent while database references remain, restore still reports success and download returns 404; a five-case data-only reference prototype detects the current-provider omission but is not shipped validation; known-good recovery restores bytes. This remaining case requires database-reference validation, not a new manifest format.

Native pre-start quick_check/nonempty-schema checks do not prove every expected application record, canonical reference or correct cross-release schema. Missing-WAL qualification uses a snapshot whose main file has no tables; checkpointed snapshots legitimately omit WAL. Native checks run after extraction, so pre-start refusal relies on verified automatic recovery rather than pre-extraction database inspection.

Sparse preflight fault: target extraction hit ENOSPC and automatic recovery failed; the exact automatic-recovery error was not separately retained in the first log. Explicit recovery capacity refusal and retained verified snapshot were asserted. A separate raw-primitive fixture/state reset restored the smaller known-good archive; that reset is not an operator recovery procedure. The fixed preflight avoids this mutation. Capacity fixtures use 96 MiB volatile tmpfs with a holder across app restarts; no disk hardware or host-reboot durability qualification.

Seven pushes racing stop were all refused/interrupted; one precommitted atomic pair restored intact. This proves stop-boundary refusal and no split pair in this run, not sustained accepted writes during capture.

Cross-deployment managed restore remains refused. Test-only second-instance transfer uses the raw production archive primitive after source authentication; no production identity-migration procedure is qualified.

Fresh-browser chat and document bodies were qualified with serialized TipTap JSON; complete browser flows/Dexie reconciliation, external provider stacks, the published release image/build graph, ARM64, production-size throughput, disk-full hardware faults and cross-release database downgrades were not qualified. The pinned production distroless base was qualified with locally built SSR output.
Injected lifecycle/filesystem failures use existing test-only seams; archives, extraction, SQLite databases, authentication, sync APIs, attachment transfer, restart and explicit recovery are real.
